newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ISRAEL, Feb 25 - No labour problems. Haifa - Four vessels discharging at berth (3 general cargo, 1 bulker). 4 Container vessels, 2 tankers. 2 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge (1 general cargo, 1 bulker), 1 container vessel, 1 tanker, 2 vessels under repair/dry-docked, 3 awaiting orders, 2 due with 1-2 days delay expected. Ashdod - 11 Vessels discharging at berth (9 general cargo, 2 bulkers). 2 Bulkers loading at berth, 3 container vessels. 9 Vessels waiting at anchorage to discharge (5 general cargo, 4 bulkers). 1 Bulker waiting to load, 3 container vessels, 1 vessel awaiting orders, 2-4 days berthing delay expected. Eilat - One tanker, 1 passenger vessel operating.

MOZAMBIQUE, Feb 24 - Nacala - Port working normally. No restrictions on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restrictions 9.5 metres at general cargo berth and 14 metres at container berth. One tug available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally. Container terminal/other terminals - Working normall 24 hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 140 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation 7.5 metres. Two tugs available.

Maputo - 24 Hour berthing/sailing for vessels up to 120 metres loa, some restrictions for larger vessels and subject to prior arrangements with port captain. All berths working normally and expected to remain so. Draft restriction in the channel is 9.0 metres less 0.5 metres (UKC) plus the rise of tide. Maximum draft for 24 hour navigation is 9 metres.
NAMIBIA, Feb 24 - Walvis Bay - Port working normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Feb 24 - Richards Bay - General cargo berths - occupied 24-25/2, but available again 27/2. Bulk import berths - Berth 701 fully committed until 26/2, berth 702 committed all week. Bulk export berths (minerals etc.) - Congested at present, with 24-48 hours berthing delay expected. Bulk coal berths - At present 15 vessels at anchorage awaiting berths/loading turn, berthing delays of 5-7 days experienced at present, due to a further 9 vessels arriving before 28/2. The delay situation is expected to remain the same for the entire week.

Durban - Container terminal - Some vessels experiencing delays of up to 48 hours, whilst others berthing on arrival. Point, New Pier, Maydon wharf berths - Working normally for general cargo vessels. Maize terminal (Maydon Wharf 8) - One maize loader expected for March. Bunker supplies - Product available but this could change daily due to bunching of vessels. Dry-dock/floating dock - Fully booked until the end of March. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths - Very busy, but no delays expected at this stage. Dry-dock - Provisionally booked from 27/2 until 15/3, thereafter open. Port Elizabeth - Working normally with no delays expected on general, ore or tanker berths. Container berth - Due to bunching of vessels on 25/2. Container vessels may incur a delay of up to 12 hours.

Cape Town - Container terminal - Delays of up to 24 hours experienced over the past weekend due to south easterly winds, but no further delays expected during the coming week. Breakbulk/general cargo berths - Working normally, with vessels berthing/operating on arrival and no delays expected. Fruit berths - Fully occupied for the coming week. Bunker berths - No delays expected. Dry-docks and repair quays - Fully booked until the end of May. For dates after that it is essential that early booking is made. Saldanha Bay - Port working normally.

TUNISIA, Feb 22 - Sfax - Six vessels in port operating of which 2 loading (1 bulk tsp, 1 bulk rock phosphate). 4 Discharging (1 general cargo, 1 bulk wheat, 1 marble, 1 gpl). Sousse - Two vessels in port of which 1 discharging marble chips, 1 awaiting orders, 1 waiting in roads but due to berth 22/2 to discharge animal fodder. Gabes - No labour problems. Three vessels loading at berth (1 cement clinker, 1 di-calcium phosphate, 1 bulk fertiliser). Tunis - Three vessels in port under arrest. Rades - Three ro-ro vessels in port.

La Goulette - North side - 1 Tanker discharging soya beans, 1 general cargo vessel, 1 passenger vessel. South side - 1 Vessel discharging grain, 1 tanker discharging lab styrene, 2 vessels in roads. Feb 24 - Bizerte - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. Three vessels in port of which 1 discharging crude oil, 1 loading steel, 1 loading cement. Zarzis - No berthing delays/congestion/strikes. No vessels in port.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Feb 16-22 - Dubai - No labour problems. 214 Vessels of which 88 containers, 12 general cargo, 5 general cargo/containers, 6 bulk carriers, 3 car carriers, 15 tankers, 7 naval vessels, 4 UAE naval vessels, 10 bunkering/under repair/taking stores etc., 1 dhow, 20 barges, 13 tugs, 22 supply boats, 2 lpg tankers, 1 crane barge, 2 passenger vessels, 1 chemical tanker, 1 survey vessel, 1 refrigerator vessel. 13 Vessels loading at berth (5 containers, 6 general cargo, 2 tankers). 8 Under repair/laid-up (1 containers, 1 general cargo, 6 tankers). 40 Vessels due (27 containers, 9 general cargo, 4 tankers) with no delays expected.

YEMEN, Feb 23 - Hodeidah - All berths occupied except No. 8. Six vessels berthed of which 1 bulk corn, 1 bulk wheat, 2 wheat flour, 1 containers, 1 general cargo, no vessels anchored. Berthing delays, general cargo/containers up to 1 day, bagged cargo up to 3 days, bulk cargo up to 5 days. Mokha - No vessels berthed, none anchored, no delays. Hodeida - Feb 24 - Seven vessels berthed of which 1 general cargo, 1 crude oil, 2 flour, 1 bagged wheat, 1 containers, 1 yellow corn, no vessels anchored. Berthing delays, containers/reefers 24 hours, general cargo (steel/timber/powder etc.) 2-3 days, bagged cargoes (sugar/rice/wheat flour etc.) 4-5 days, bulk wheat/corn 5-7 days.
